ideal: Qxg5 allows ...Rh8, forcing Qxh8+ Kxh8 and then Nf6 to prevent mate on h7.
note: The queen sacrifice does not end the danger: the h7 mate threat also costs the knight.

ideal: Qg5 misses Qf4, when Qxh5 threatens mate on h8 and ...Qh7 allows Qxg5+, winning two pawns.
note: The h8 threat appears after Qxh5 and helps collect the second pawn.

ideal: Bd2 misses Nd5, when Nxc7+ forks the king and a8-rook, allowing Nxa8.
note: The rook fork is the point; losing castling rights is incidental.

ideal: Bb3 misses Bxf7+ Kxf7 Qxd7, exchanging bishops while winning the f7-pawn.
note: The checking capture draws the king away from the d7-bishop and also prevents castling.

ideal: Qe1+ lets Rf1 save the f6-rook before ...Qxg5 Qxg5, leaving only a knight for your queen.
note: No pawn falls in the cited exchange, and the h7 mate threat also occurs in the best line.

ideal: Qg7 misses Rxf2, threatening mate on h2.
note: Taking f2 creates the decisive attack; the extra pawn is secondary.

ideal: h6 misses Bxf2+ Kxf2 Ng4+ Ke1 Qxg5, recovering the bishop and winning the f2-pawn.
note: The checks recover the sacrificed bishop while leaving White unable to castle.

ideal: Bg5 misses Nxe5, winning the e5-pawn with a mate threat on f7.
note: Nxe5 both takes a pawn and threatens Bxf7 mate; ...Be6 answers the threat.

ideal: c3 loses the c-pawn to ...Qb6 and ...Bxc3, with the b2-pawn pinned and mate threatened on b2.
note: The b-file pin prevents bxc3, and the mate threat forces White to defend.

ideal: Rg8 allows Nf6, threatening mate on d7 and forcing ...Nc6 R1xc6 before ...Rxg7 Rxg7.
note: The d7 mate threat forces the knight concession; the final exchange also costs Black a rook.

ideal: h3 allows Nxc2+ Kf1 Nxe3+, winning your queen and c2-pawn for a knight.
note: The checking knight fork wins the queen; the castling loss adds little to that explanation.

ideal: Rg8 misses Qd6, threatening mate on h2 before ...Qxc6 takes the knight after Bg3.
note: The mate threat gives Black time to capture the otherwise mobile c6-knight.

ideal: Qxg5 allows Qxf7+ Kd8 Qf8+ Kd7 Qxa8, losing a rook and pawn for your bishop.
note: The queen checks displace the king before taking the a8-rook.

ideal: Ne5+ misses Qd5+, which leads to Qf5 mate after the knight checks drive the king to f6.
note: The missed mating line is decisive; the knight loss and easily parried g2 threat obscure it.

ideal: Bh7+ loses your bishop because Qxb2 is answered by ...Nd3+ Ke2 Nxb2, recovering Black's queen.
note: The knight fork cancels the apparent queen win, leaving the bishop sacrifice uncompensated.

ideal: Rh1 allows b4 and ...Rxd5 Qxd5, threatening mate on a8 so ...h6 leaves the h5-knight to Qxh5.
note: The mate threat costs a defensive tempo, so Black loses the knight after exchanging the rook for White's knight.

ideal: Rxg3 misses c6, threatening mate on b5 and winning the knight after Nc3 b5+ Nxb5 cxb5+.
note: The mate threat draws the knight into the pawn sacrifice; later pawn captures balance the pawn losses.

ideal: Bf5 misses Bxh5, when Qxh5 Qxg3 Kf1 Be3 threatens mate on g2.
note: The knight exchange and pawn capture lead to an attack that demands Re2.

ideal: Nf6+ misses Rxd7 Rxd7 Nf6+ Kg7 Qxa8, winning a knight overall.
note: The rook captures cancel, leaving a knight gained; the g8 mate threat is an additional tempo.

ideal: Qg8 leaves the e7-bishop undefended after Nd6+ Kb8 Qxe7.
note: The discovered queen attack wins the bishop, with a further mate threat on b7.

ideal: Bf4 allows Nxf4, threatening mate on d2; Rxe5+ and Nd6+ only delay ...Rxb2 mate.
note: The material sacrifices prolong a mating attack rather than explain its cause.

ideal: Qd5 allows Nxc7+ Kd8 Nxd5, losing your queen and c7-pawn.
note: The knight forks king and queen; castling rights are incidental.

ideal: Bh4 allows Bb4+ Qd2 Bxd2+ Kxd2, losing your queen for a bishop.
note: The queen loss is decisive, making the castling consequence incidental.

ideal: Rf4 loses a rook for a pawn after ...Nxf4 Nxe4 Qxe4 Bb4+ Kg8 exf4.
note: The knight captures eventually cancel; the temporary g2 threat does not prevent exf4.

ideal: Bd6 misses Bg4, whose mate threat on d1 drives the f3-rook to d3 before ...Bf5 Rxd8 Raxd8 wins it.
note: The cited sequence wins a rook for a pawn after the queens cancel; the bishop is only lost later.

ideal: Qf3 misses e6, threatening mate on g7 and winning queen for bishop after ...Bf6 Bxf6 Qxf6 exf7+ Qxf7 Bxf7+ Kxf7.
note: The mating threat provokes the bishop block, then the discovered check forces the queen onto f7.

ideal: e4 misses O-O, when Qxd6 and the exchanges ending Nxd6+ win the d6-pawn.
note: The material gain survives the exchanges; Black's central king is much less significant once the queens are gone.

ideal: Qg6+ misses Re1 and Rxe6, threatening mate on h6 and meeting ...Bxf2+ Kh2 Bxg3+ with Kxg3.
note: The rook capture creates the h6 mate threat, and Black sacrifices the bishop for checking time.

ideal: Na5 loses the f7-pawn after Bxf7+ Ke7 Qa4 Kxf7 Qxa5.
note: The bishop and knight exchange leaves White a pawn up, with Black also unable to castle.

ideal: Qg4 allows Rfxf2, threatening mate on h2 and forcing Rg2, when ...Qxg4 hxg4 Rxg2 wins the rook.
note: The mate threat forces the rook onto g2, and the later checking capture also wins the d2-rook.
